title.zh: 卷246 列傳三十三 谭泰 何洛会 锡图库 博尔辉 冷僧机
title.en: Volume 246 Biographies 33: Tan Tai, He Luohui, Xi Tu Ku, Bo Er Hui, Leng Sengji
title.raw: 卷246 列傳三十三 谭泰 何洛会 锡图库 博尔辉 冷僧机

sentences.zh: =譚泰=譚泰，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正黃旗人，揚古利從弟也。

translations.literal: Tan Tai — Tan Tai, of the Sumuru clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, was Yangguli's younger cousin on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai, of the Sumuru clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and was Yangguli's younger paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 初授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed niru ejen (company commander).
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed niru commander.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，擢巴牙喇章京，與固山額真圖爾格分統左右翼兵，略錦州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was promoted to bayara janggin, and with gushan ejen Thurgai jointly commanded the left and right wing troops in a raid on Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong (1634), he was raised to vanguard officer and, together with banner commander Thurgai, led the left and right wings in operations against Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 還從太宗伐明，自上方堡毀邊牆以入，敗明兵，克保安州。

translations.literal: Returning, he followed Taizong in a campaign against Ming, entered by destroying the border wall at Shangfang Fort, defeated Ming troops, and captured Bao'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he accompanied Taizong (Hong Taiji) against the Ming, breaching the border wall at Shangfang Fort to enter, routing Ming forces and taking Bao'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢巴牙喇纛章京，令關白諸事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to bayara tuwakiyara janggin and ordered to report all matters to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to chief vanguard standard-bearer and charged with reporting everything directly to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 九年，揚古利賜第，侍衛宗室濟馬護欲得其舊居，揚古利不可。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Yangguli was granted a residence; Jimahu of the imperial guard clansmen wished to obtain his former dwelling, but Yangguli would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1635), when Yangguli received an imperial mansion, Jimahu of the guard corps tried to take over his old quarters, but Yangguli refused.

sentences.zh: 濟馬護囑譚泰入奏，譚泰匿不以聞，濟馬護訴於上，上責譚泰曰：「爾為朕耳目，凡事當無隱。

translations.literal: Jimahu had Tan Tai memorialize the throne on his behalf; Tan Tai concealed it and did not report it. Jimahu complained to the emperor, and the emperor rebuked Tan Tai, saying: "You are my eyes and ears; in all matters you should conceal nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Jimahu asked Tan Tai to bring the matter before the throne, but Tan Tai kept it secret. When Jimahu appealed directly to the emperor, the latter rebuked Tan Tai: "You are my eyes and ears; nothing should be hidden from me."

sentences.zh: 濟馬護乃朕叔父之子，其言尚不能達，民間勞苦嗟怨，何由得使朕知？

translations.literal: Jimahu is the son of my uncle; even his words cannot reach me — how then can I know of the labor and grievances of the common people?
translations.idiomatic: "Jimahu is my uncle's own son, yet his words cannot reach me — how am I to learn of the people's toil and complaints?"

sentences.zh: 爾恃宗族強盛，欺陵愚弱，朕所深惡！

translations.literal: You rely on the power of your clan and bully the foolish and weak — this is what I deeply detest!
translations.idiomatic: "You lean on your clan's strength to oppress the weak — that is what I abhor above all!"

sentences.zh: 」下刑部質訊，奪官。

translations.literal: He was sent down to the Board of Punishments for examination and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed over to the Board of Punishments for investigation and dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 尋复授本旗固山額真。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed gushan ejen of his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was restored as banner commander of his own banner.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從武英郡王阿濟格等伐明，克延慶等十二城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Ying Ajige and others in a campaign against Ming and took twelve cities including Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636) he joined Prince Ying Ajige's expedition against the Ming and captured twelve cities, Yanqing among them.

sentences.zh: 進圍定興，先登有功。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Dingxing, he was first to scale the walls with merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Dingxing he led the assault over the walls with distinction.

sentences.zh: 復與固山額真阿山等設伏，敗明遵化三屯營守兵，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Again, with gushan ejen Ashan and others he laid an ambush, defeated the Ming garrison at Zunhua's Santun Camp, and annihilated them completely.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined banner commander Ashan in an ambush that routed and wiped out the Ming defenders at Santun Camp near Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 師還，宴勞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, a feast was given to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return a celebratory feast was held in their honor.

sentences.zh: 復從上伐朝鮮，朝鮮王棄城走，譚泰率師入其城，盡收其輜重。

translations.literal: Again he followed the emperor in a campaign against Korea; the King of Korea abandoned the city and fled. Tan Tai led the army into the capital and seized all its baggage and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor into Korea; when the Korean king fled his capital, Tan Tai entered the city and seized all military stores.

sentences.zh: 從上逐朝鮮王至南漢城，受降而還。

translations.literal: Following the emperor he pursued the King of Korea to Namhansung, accepted his surrender, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Korean king to Namhansung, witnessed his surrender, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 四年，從睿親王多爾袞等伐明，與固山額真葉臣自太平寨破青山口，與明兵十三戰，皆捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Prince Rui Dorgon and others in a campaign against Ming; with gushan ejen Yečen he broke through Qingshan Pass from Taiping Stockade and fought thirteen battles with Ming troops, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1639) he joined Prince Rui Dorgon's Ming campaign; with banner commander Yečen he broke through Qingshan Pass from Taiping Stockade and won all thirteen engagements with Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍鞏阿岱，濟馬護兄也，譚泰與相詬於禁門，坐罰。

translations.literal: Fuyu Guo Gong Adažai was Jimahu's elder brother; Tan Tai exchanged insults with him at the forbidden gate and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Prince Gong Adažai, Jimahu's elder brother, quarreled with Tan Tai at the palace gate, and Tan Tai was penalized.

sentences.zh: 六年，從圍錦州，譚泰將四百人自小凌河直抵海濱，絕明兵歸路。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he joined the siege of Jinzhou; Tan Tai led four hundred men from the Xiao Ling River straight to the seashore, cutting off the Ming army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1641), during the siege of Jinzhou, he took four hundred men down the Xiao Ling River to the coast and cut off the Ming army's escape route.

sentences.zh: 與明總督洪承疇兵戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: He fought the troops of Ming Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He engaged Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou's army and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 授世職二等參將。

translations.literal: He was granted a hereditary office of second-rank deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He received a hereditary rank equivalent to second-class deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，從輔國公篇古等攻薊州，擊敗明總兵白騰蛟、白廣恩等，俘馘為諸軍最。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Fuguo Gong Panggu and others in attacking Jizhou, defeated Ming regional commanders Bai Tengjiao and Bai Guang'en and others, and his captives and heads taken were the most of any army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Fuguo Gong Panggu's attack on Jizhou, defeated regional commanders Bai Tengjiao and Bai Guang'en, and took more prisoners and heads than any other unit.

sentences.zh: 八年，命率銳卒與固山額真準塔更番戍錦州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to lead crack troops with gushan ejen Zhuntai in rotating garrison duty at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he and banner commander Zhuntai were ordered to rotate crack troops in the Jinzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，逐破李自成於慶都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes and pursued and defeated Li Zicheng at Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 (1644) he crossed into China proper and routed Li Zicheng at Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 復將巴牙喇兵躡擊，至真定，大破之，敘功授一等公。

translations.literal: Again he led bayara troops in pursuit, reaching Zhending, where he inflicted a great defeat; for his merit he was granted the rank of duke of the first class.
translations.idiomatic: He led vanguard troops in pursuit to Zhending, broke Li's forces again, and was rewarded with a first-class dukedom for his service.

sentences.zh: 睿親王攝政，譚泰與巴牙喇纛章京圖賴、啟心郎索尼並見信任。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui served as regent, Tan Tai together with bayara tuwakiyara janggin Tülai and Kesin Sony were all trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Rui's regency Tan Tai shared the regent's confidence with chief vanguard Tülai and Kesin (adviser) Sony.

sentences.zh: 固山額真何洛會誣肅親王豪格怨譚泰等不附己，訐之睿親王，王謂譚泰忠，益信任之。

translations.literal: Gushan ejen Heluohui falsely accused Prince Su Hooge of resenting Tan Tai and others for not siding with him and reported this to Prince Rui; the Prince said Tan Tai was loyal and trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Banner commander Heluohui falsely told Prince Rui that Prince Su Hooge resented Tan Tai and others for refusing to join him; the regent pronounced Tan Tai loyal and relied on him even more.

sentences.zh: 大學士希福忤譚泰，希福欲易賜第，譚泰不可，希福誚之，益怒。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xifu offended Tan Tai; Xifu wished to exchange his granted residence, Tan Tai would not permit it, Xifu mocked him, and [Tan Tai] grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xifu crossed Tan Tai; when Xifu sought to swap his imperial residence Tan Tai refused, Xifu taunted him, and Tan Tai's rage only grew.

sentences.zh: 其弟譚布以希福述睿親王自言過誤告譚泰，譚泰訐之法司，希福坐黜。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tan Bu reported to Tan Tai that Xifu had related Prince Rui's own admissions of error; Tan Tai reported this to the legal bureau, and Xifu was dismissed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai's brother Tan Bu told him that Xifu had repeated Prince Rui's own confessions of fault; Tan Tai denounced this to the judicial authorities and Xifu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二年，英親王阿濟格坐奏軍事不實得罪，命譚泰與鰲拜等集眾宣其罪。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Ying Ajige was guilty of reporting military affairs untruthfully and was ordered to have Tan Tai together with Oboi and others assemble the multitude and proclaim his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1645) Prince Ying Ajige was punished for misreporting military affairs; Tan Tai and Oboi were ordered to assemble the troops and announce his crimes.

sentences.zh: 譚泰匿諭旨不以示眾，索尼發其罪，降世職昂邦章京，奪官。

translations.literal: Tan Tai concealed the imperial edict and did not show it to the multitude; Sony exposed his crime, and he was demoted to hereditary Angbang janggin and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai hid the edict instead of reading it aloud; Sony exposed him, and he was demoted to hereditary Angbang janggin and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 譚泰怨索尼，訐索尼於內庫牧馬鼓琴及禁門橋下捕魚，索尼亦坐黜。

translations.literal: Tan Tai resented Sony and reported that Sony pastured horses and played zither in the inner treasury and fished under the bridge at the forbidden gate; Sony was also dismissed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai retaliated by denouncing Sony for keeping horses and playing music in the inner storehouse and fishing under the palace bridge; Sony was dismissed too.

sentences.zh: 譚泰復起為本旗固山額真。

translations.literal: Tan Tai was again raised up as gushan ejen of his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai was soon restored as banner commander of his own banner.

sentences.zh: 初，師下江南，譚泰自西安逐捕流寇，慮不與平江南功，使謂圖賴曰：「我軍道迂險，後至。

translations.literal: At first, when the army descended on Jiangnan, Tan Tai from Xi'an pursued and captured bandits, fearing he would not share in the merit of pacifying Jiangnan; he sent word to Tülai saying: "Our army's route is circuitous and dangerous; we will arrive late."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as forces moved south, Tan Tai was chasing bandits from Xi'an and feared missing credit for pacifying the south. He sent Tülai a message: "Our route is long and treacherous; we will arrive late."

sentences.zh: 今南京未下，請留待我軍。

translations.literal: Now Nanjing has not yet fallen; please wait for our army."
translations.idiomatic: "Nanjing has not fallen yet — please hold until we arrive."

sentences.zh: 」圖賴書告索尼，使啟睿親王，或發觀之，懼譚泰得罪，毀其書勿使達索尼。

translations.literal: Tülai wrote informing Sony, wishing to report to Prince Rui; someone opened and saw it, feared Tan Tai would be punished, destroyed the letter and did not let it reach Sony.
translations.idiomatic: Tülai wrote to Sony to inform the regent; someone intercepted the letter, fearing Tan Tai's ruin, destroyed it before it reached Sony.

sentences.zh: 圖賴師還，詰索尼，發其事，王鞫齎書者，得狀。

translations.literal: When Tülai's army returned he questioned Sony; the matter was exposed; the Prince examined the letter-bearer and obtained the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Tülai returned he confronted Sony; the affair came to light, and the regent interrogated the messenger and established the facts.

sentences.zh: 譚泰又坐與婦翁固山額真阿山遣巫者治病。

translations.literal: Tan Tai was again guilty of sending a shaman to heal illness together with his father-in-law gushan ejen Ashan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai was further implicated for having Ashan, his father-in-law and a banner commander, employ a shaman to treat illness.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣議罪，論死，下獄，王使視之，並餽食焉。

translations.literal: He was sent down for the court officials to deliberate punishment; death was decided and he was imprisoned; the Prince sent someone to see him and even provided food.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated and sentenced him to death; in prison the regent sent attendants—and even food.

sentences.zh: 譚泰曰：「王若拯我，我殺身報王！

translations.literal: Tan Tai said: "If the Prince saves me, I will give my life to repay the Prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai said, "If Your Highness saves me, I will repay you with my life!"

sentences.zh: 」乃出之獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was then released.

sentences.zh: 五年，復原官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1648) his former offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛江西，授譚泰征南大將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi; Tan Tai was appointed Grand General for the Southern Expedition and led an army to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi, Tan Tai was made southern expedition commander-general and marched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 聲桓以步騎七萬人抗我師，譚泰督諸軍與戰，次九江，大敗聲桓兵，獲其舟以濟師。

translations.literal: Shenghuan with seventy thousand infantry and cavalry resisted our army; Tan Tai supervised the various armies in battle; at Jiujiang he heavily defeated Shenghuan's troops and seized his boats to ferry the army across.
translations.idiomatic: Shenghuan met him with seventy thousand foot and horse; at Jiujiang Tan Tai routed his army and seized his boats to ferry the Qing forces.

sentences.zh: 攻南昌，為長圍困之，數月，麾將士以雲梯登，聲桓中二矢，投水死；

translations.literal: Attacking Nanchang, he made a long siege encircling it; after several months he directed officers and soldiers to ascend on cloud ladders; Shenghuan was struck by two arrows and threw himself into the water and died;
translations.idiomatic: He laid siege to Nanchang for months, then ordered assault ladders; Shenghuan took two arrows and drowned himself;

sentences.zh: 又破其將王得仁。

translations.literal: He also defeated his general Wang Deren.
translations.idiomatic: and defeated his general Wang Deren.

sentences.zh: 南康、瑞州、臨江、袁州並下。

translations.literal: Nankang, Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Yuanzhou all fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang, Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Yuanzhou fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 當聲桓叛時，李成棟以廣東應之，南昌圍急，成棟赴援。

translations.literal: When Shenghuan rebelled, Li Chengdong responded from Guangdong; as the siege of Nanchang grew urgent, Li Chengdong came to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengdong rose in Guangdong to support the rebellion; as Nanchang tightened, he marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 譚泰師將至贛州，聞成棟入信豐，譚泰遣諸將乘勝襲擊，成棟兵潰，溺水死，克信豐。

translations.literal: Tan Tai's army was about to reach Ganzhou; hearing that Chengdong had entered Xinfeng, Tan Tai dispatched generals to strike while victory was hot; Chengdong's army collapsed, he drowned and died, and Xinfeng was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Near Ganzhou Tan Tai learned Chengdong was at Xinfeng; he sent generals in pursuit, Chengdong's army broke, he drowned, and Xinfeng was taken.

sentences.zh: 別將徇撫州、建昌。

translations.literal: Separate generals subjugated Fuzhou and Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Other columns pacified Fuzhou and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 江西悉平。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，授一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted a first-class jingqi nihačan (hereditary baron).
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made a first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 七年，睿親王薨，上命吏、刑、工三部增設滿洲尚書各一，授譚泰吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Rui died; the emperor ordered that the Boards of Civil Office, Punishments, and Works each add one Manchu minister, and Tan Tai was appointed Minister of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1650), after Prince Rui's death, the emperor added a Manchu minister to each of the Civil, Punishments, and Works boards and appointed Tan Tai Minister of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，追論睿親王罪狀，大學士剛林、祁充格皆坐誅，罪不及譚泰。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Shizu emperor personally took power; Prince Rui's crimes were reviewed posthumously, and Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were both executed, but the crimes did not extend to Tan Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1651) the Shunzhi emperor assumed personal rule; Prince Rui was posthumously condemned and Grand Secretaries Ganglin and Qi Chongge were executed, but Tan Tai was not implicated.

sentences.zh: 時圖賴已卒，索尼方罪廢，譚泰毀圖賴墓室，洩舊忿。

translations.literal: At that time Tülai had already died and Sony was just now under punishment and dismissal; Tan Tai destroyed Tülai's tomb chamber to vent old resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tülai was already dead and Sony was under punishment; Tan Tai desecrated Tülai's tomb to settle an old grudge.

sentences.zh: 五月，御史張煊劾大學士陳名夏等，下王大臣會鞫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Censor Zhang Huang impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia and others; the case was sent to princes and grand ministers for joint examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Censor Zhang Huang impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia and others; the case went to a tribunal of princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 譚泰袒名夏，讞上，命未下，譚泰前奏，言煊劾皆虛，且所舉諸事皆在赦前，煊以外轉嫌，誣名夏等死罪，當反坐，煊遂見法。

translations.literal: Tan Tai favored Mingxia; when the verdict was submitted and the order had not yet been issued, Tan Tai advanced to memorialize that Huang's impeachments were all false, and moreover the matters he cited were all before the amnesty; Huang, transferring hatred outward from other grievances, falsely charged Mingxia and others with capital crimes and ought to suffer反坐; Huang was then executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai shielded Chen Mingxia; before sentence was pronounced he argued that Zhang Huang's charges were false and referred to matters already amnestied; alleging capital crimes on that basis, he said Huang should suffer the penalty he had sought to impose — and Huang was executed.

sentences.zh: 譚泰愈縱恣，岳爾多其妻弟也，襲一等精奇尼哈番，為奪其族人法喀應襲一等阿思哈尼哈番合併為三等侯；

translations.literal: Tan Tai grew ever more arrogant; Yue'erduo was his wife's younger brother and inherited a first-class jingqi nihačan; for him Tan Tai seized his clansman Faka's rightful inheritance of a first-class ashahanihačan and merged them into a third-class marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Growing bolder, Tan Tai arranged for his brother-in-law Yue'erduo, who held a first-class barony, to seize clansman Faka's first-class viscounty and merge the two into a third-class marquisate;

sentences.zh: 佟圖賴其女弟之夫也，時金礪駐防杭州，妄稱員缺，以佟圖賴擬補。

translations.literal: Totoi was his younger sister's husband; at the time Jin Li was garrisoned at Hangzhou and falsely claimed a vacancy, nominating Totoi to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Totoi was married to his sister; when Jin Li was stationed at Hangzhou he falsely declared a vacancy and proposed Totoi to fill it.

sentences.zh: 上自譚泰袒陳名夏構張煊，心厭惡之。

translations.literal: From the time Tan Tai shielded Chen Mingxia and framed Zhang Huang, the emperor's heart held disgust for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Tan Tai had protected Chen Mingxia and destroyed Zhang Huang, the emperor had grown to loathe him.

sentences.zh: 是歲八月，下詔責其專橫，命執付獄，集廷臣議罪。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month an edict was issued reproaching his despotism; he was ordered seized and committed to prison, and court officials assembled to deliberate his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict condemned his arrogance; he was arrested and the court assembled to judge him.

sentences.zh: 鰲拜复訐譚泰阿附睿親王及營私擅政諸狀，讞皆實。

translations.literal: Oboi again reported Tan Tai's leaning toward Prince Rui and various acts of personal gain and arbitrary governance; the verdict found all true.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi further denounced Tan Tai's favoritism toward Prince Rui and private abuses; every charge was upheld.

sentences.zh: 王大臣議誅譚泰及其子孫，上命誅譚泰，籍其家，子孫貸連坐。

translations.literal: Princes and grand ministers deliberated executing Tan Tai and his descendants; the emperor ordered Tan Tai executed, his household confiscated, and his descendants spared collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The tribunal recommended death for Tan Tai and his line; the emperor executed Tan Tai and seized his property but spared his descendants collective punishment.

sentences.zh: =何洛會=何洛會，失其氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Heluohui — Heluohui, his clan name lost, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Heluohui — his clan name is unrecorded; he was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父阿吉賴，事太祖，從征戰，官牛錄額真。

translations.literal: His father Ajilai served Taizu, followed campaigns, and held the office of niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ajilai served Taizu, fought in campaigns, and held the rank of company commander.

sentences.zh: 卒，何洛會嗣，兼巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When he died Heluohui succeeded him and also held the post of bayara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: On his death Heluohui succeeded him and also served as vanguard company officer.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，從伐明，略錦州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he followed a campaign against Ming and raided Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he joined the Ming campaign and operated against Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔免諸功臣徭役，何洛會與焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict exempted all meritorious officials from corvée labor; Heluohui was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year meritorious ministers were exempted from corvée; Heluohui was included.

sentences.zh: 崇德五年，授正黃旗蒙古固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongde he was appointed gushan ejen of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 5 he became commander of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 從睿親王多爾袞伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Rui Dorgon in a campaign against Ming and besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Rui Dorgon's Ming expedition and besieged Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 調滿洲固山額真。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Manchu gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command a Manchu banner.

sentences.zh: 七年，錦州既下，追論圍錦州時何洛會匿鄂羅塞臣破陣功，當奪官，上宥之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, after Jinzhou had fallen, it was reviewed that during the Jinzhou siege Heluohui had concealed Orosencen's merit in breaking the enemy line; his office ought to have been stripped, but the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Jinzhou fell, Heluohui was found to have suppressed Orosencen's credit for breaking the enemy line; though liable to dismissal, the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 何洛會隸肅親王豪格，頗見任使。

translations.literal: Heluohui was under Prince Su Hooge and was quite employed and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Heluohui served under Prince Su Hooge and enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，睿親王攝政，與肅親王有隙。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Prince Rui served as regent and had a rift with Prince Su.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi emperor's accession Prince Rui regented and clashed with Prince Su.

sentences.zh: 何洛會訐肅親王與兩黃旗大臣揚善、俄莫克圖、伊成格、羅碩將謀亂，肅親王坐削爵，揚善等皆棄市。

translations.literal: Heluohui reported that Prince Su together with grand ministers of the two Yellow Banners Yangshan, Emektu, Icengge, and Luoshuo planned rebellion; Prince Su was stripped of his princedom, and Yangshan and others were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Heluohui accused Prince Su and Yellow Banner ministers Yangshan, Emektu, Icengge, and Luoshuo of plotting rebellion; Prince Su lost his title and the ministers were executed.

sentences.zh: 賞何洛會告姦，籍俄莫克圖、伊成格家畀之，授世職二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Heluohui was rewarded for denouncing treachery; the households of Emektu and Icengge were confiscated and given to him, and he was granted a hereditary office of second-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for the denunciation, he received the confiscated estates of Emektu and Icengge and a second-class company commander's hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 尋從睿親王入關，擊李自成，逐至慶都。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Prince Rui through the passes, struck Li Zicheng, and pursued him to Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Prince Rui south, fought Li Zicheng, and pursued him to Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 還，睿親王令奉表迎世祖，擢內大臣，留守盛京。

translations.literal: Returning, Prince Rui ordered him to present a memorial welcoming Shizu, promoted him to inner grand minister, and left him to guard Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Prince Rui sent him to welcome the young emperor; he was made inner grand minister and left to guard the old capital.

sentences.zh: 阿哈尼堪將左翼，碩詹將右翼，並於熊耀城、錦州、寧遠、鳳凰城、興京、義州、新城、牛莊、岫岩城各置城守官，皆統於何洛會。

translations.literal: Ahanikan commanded the left wing and Suozhan the right wing; at Xiongyao Fort, Jinzhou, Ningyuan, Fenghuang Fort, Xingjing, Yizhou, Xincheng, Niuzhuang, and Xiuyan Fort city garrison commanders were each placed, all under Heluohui's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Ahanikan led the left wing and Suozhan the right; garrison commanders were posted at Xiongyao, Jinzhou, Ningyuan, Fenghuang, Xingjing, Yizhou, Xincheng, Niuzhuang, and Xiuyan — all under Heluohui.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，敘功，進世職一等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi merits were reviewed and his hereditary office was advanced to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 his service was recognized with promotion to a first-class hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 旋命率師駐防西安，道河南，討定西平土寇劉洪起等。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Xi'an, by way of Henan to suppress Western Pacification district local bandits Liu Hongqi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to garrison Xi'an, marching through Henan to suppress bandits such as Liu Hongqi in Dingxi ping.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月，授定西大將軍，命自陝西徇四川。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month he was appointed Grand General for the Pacification of the West and ordered from Shaanxi to advance into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made western pacification commander-general with orders to enter Sichuan from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時自成將劉體純等犯商州，叛將賀珍與其黨孫守法、胡向宸等分據漢中、興安。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng's general Liu Tichun and others attacked Shangzhou; rebel general He Zhen with his partisans Sun Shoufa, Hu Xiangchen, and others separately held Hanzhong and Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's general Liu Tichun was raiding Shangzhou; the rebel He Zhen and allies Sun Shoufa and Hu Xiangchen held Hanzhong and Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 三年，珍以七萬人犯西安，何洛會督兵迎戰，珍敗走，复逐破之，並破體純商州。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhen with seventy thousand men attacked Xi'an; Heluohui supervised troops to meet the battle; Zhen was defeated and fled; he was again pursued and broken, and Liu Tichun was also broken at Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year He Zhen attacked Xi'an with seventy thousand men; Heluohui defeated and pursued him and also broke Liu Tichun at Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 肅親王從入關，破李自成，复爵。

translations.literal: Prince Su followed through the passes, defeated Li Zicheng, and had his princedom restored.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su had followed the armies south, defeated Li Zicheng, and regained his title.

sentences.zh: 至是，上命為靖遠大將軍，下四川，召何洛會還京師。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor appointed him Grand General for the Pacification of the Distant West to descend on Sichuan and summoned Heluohui back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now made Prince Su distant-pacification commander-general for Sichuan and recalled Heluohui to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，命率師駐防宣府，仍授正黃旗滿洲固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Xuanfu and was again appointed Manchu gushan ejen of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posted to Xuanfu and again given the Plain Yellow Manchu banner command.

sentences.zh: 五年，調鑲白旗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he transferred to the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 命佐譚泰定江西，擊破金聲桓、王得仁、李成棟，事具譚泰傳。

translations.literal: He was ordered to assist Tan Tai in pacifying Jiangxi, defeating Jin Shenghuan, Wang Deren, and Li Chengdong; the affairs are detailed in Tan Tai's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Tan Tai in pacifying Jiangxi, defeating Jin Shenghuan, Wang Deren, and Li Chengdong — as recounted in Tan Tai's biography.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜所獲金銀珠玉，進世職三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted the gold, silver, pearls, and jades captured, and his hereditary office was advanced to third-rank jingqi nihačan.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received captured gold, silver, and jewels and was raised to third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 肅親王師還，貝子屯齊等訐王諸悖妄狀，何洛會復從而證之，遂坐奪爵，以幽系終。

translations.literal: When Prince Su's army returned, Beile Tunqi and others reported various rebellious and presumptuous acts of the Prince; Heluohui again followed in testifying to them; thereupon he was sentenced to strip his princedom and ended in secret imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Su's return, Beile Tunqi impeached him for many offenses; Heluohui testified again, and the prince lost his title and died under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 睿親王取肅親王福金，召肅親王諸子入府校射，何洛會詈之曰：「見此鬼魅，不覺心悸！

translations.literal: Prince Rui took Prince Su's princess consort Fujin, summoned Prince Su's sons into the mansion for archery practice, and Heluohui cursed them, saying: "Seeing these specters, one cannot but feel the heart tremble!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui took Prince Su's consort and summoned Su's sons to shoot in his mansion; Heluohui cursed them: "These demons make my heart quail!"

sentences.zh: 」尚書譚泰聞其語。

translations.literal: Minister Tan Tai heard his words.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Tan Tai heard what he said.

sentences.zh: 及睿親王薨，世祖親政，何洛會語貝子錫翰曰：「兩黃旗大臣與我相惡，我嘗訐告肅親王，今豈肯容我？

translations.literal: When Prince Rui died and Shizu personally took power, Heluohui said to Beile Xihan: "The grand ministers of the two Yellow Banners hate me; I once reported Prince Su — will they now be willing to bear with me?"
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Rui's death and the emperor's personal rule, Heluohui told Beile Xihan: "The Yellow Banner ministers hate me — I denounced Prince Su once; will they spare me now?"

sentences.zh: 」八年二月，蘇克薩哈等訐睿親王將率兩白旗移駐永平，且私具上服禦，及薨用斂，何洛會、羅什、博爾惠等皆知狀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year Suksaha and others reported that Prince Rui was about to lead the two White Banners to transfer garrison to Yongping, and had privately prepared imperial robes for himself, and at death used them for burial; Heluohui, Rosi, Bo'erhui, and others all knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year Suksaha charged that Prince Rui had planned to move the White Banners to Yongping, secretly prepared imperial regalia, and was buried in it; Heluohui, Rosi, Bo'erhui, and others knew of this.

sentences.zh: 時羅什、博爾惠已先誅，執何洛會，下王大臣會鞫。

translations.literal: At that time Rosi and Bo'erhui had already been executed first; Heluohui was seized and sent to princes and grand ministers for joint examination.
translations.idiomatic: Rosi and Bo'erhui were already dead; Heluohui was arrested and tried by the princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 譚泰、錫翰各以何洛會語告，又追論誣告肅親王罪，與其兄胡錫並磔死，籍其家。

translations.literal: Tan Tai and Xihan each reported Heluohui's words; his crime of falsely accusing Prince Su was also reviewed; he and his elder brother Huxi were both executed by dismemberment, and their household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai and Xihan repeated his confession; for the false charge against Prince Su he and his brother Huxi were dismembered and their property seized.

sentences.zh: =錫圖庫=錫圖庫，烏扎拉氏，滿洲正白旗人，世居烏拉。

translations.literal: Xitu Ku — Xitu Ku, of the Ujala clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner, whose family had long dwelt at Ula.
translations.idiomatic: Xitu Ku, of the Ujala clan, was a Plain White Banner Manchu whose family came from Ula.

sentences.zh: 兄福蘭，當太祖時來歸，授世職備禦。

translations.literal: His elder brother Fulan came to submit in the time of Taizu and was granted a hereditary office of beiyu (guard).
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Fulan submitted in Taizu's reign and received a hereditary guard's rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，錫圖庫嗣，授牛錄額真，兼巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When [Fulan] died, Xitu Ku succeeded [to his office], was appointed niru commander, and concurrently served as bayara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother died, Xitu Ku inherited the family rank and was made niru commander while also holding the office of bayara jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，師克永平，錫圖庫與甲喇額真圖魯什等率兵循徼，得邏卒二、馬十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, the army captured Yongping; Xitu Ku with jalan commander Tursi and others led troops on patrol and obtained two Ming deserters and seventeen horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancong (1630), when the army took Yongping, Xitu Ku and jalan commander Tursi led patrols and brought back two Ming defectors and seventeen horses.

sentences.zh: 五年，诇敵大凌河，得二人以還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he scouted the enemy at Dalinghe and brought back two men.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he reconnoitered enemy positions at Dalinghe and returned with two captives.

sentences.zh: 上伐明，圍大凌河城，敗錦州援兵，錫圖庫皆有功。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Ming, besieged Dalinghe city, and defeated Jinzhou relief troops, Xitu Ku had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaigns against the Ming—the siege of Dalinghe and the rout of Jinzhou's relief forces—he distinguished himself throughout.

sentences.zh: 六年，復從伐明，略宣府、大同邊外，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again followed a campaign against Ming, raided outside the borders of Xuanfu and Datong, and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1632) he again joined a Ming expedition, harrying the lands beyond Xuanfu and Datong and returning with heavy loot and many slain.

sentences.zh: 八年，复略蒙古錫爾哈、錫伯圖諸地，斬七十餘級、俘百餘戶及馬駝，賚以所獲，進世職一等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again raided the Mongol lands of Xierha, Xibotu, and elsewhere, beheading more than seventy and capturing more than a hundred households along with horses and camels; he was rewarded with part of the booty and advanced in hereditary office to first-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1634) he raided the Mongol districts of Xierha and Xibotu, killing over seventy and taking more than a hundred households with horses and camels; for this he received a share of the spoils and was promoted to first-rank hereditary jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕噶布什賢噶喇依昂邦勞薩等略明邊，入長城，攻代、朔諸州，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, together with Gabsihiyan rankanggin Angbang Laosa and others, he raided the Ming border, entered the Great Wall, attacked the prefectures of Dai and Shuo, and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1635) he joined Gabsihiyan officers Laosa and others in a border raid, broke through the Great Wall, stormed Dai and Shuo, and won extensive kills and booty.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，睿親王多爾袞率師伐明，攻寧遠，錫圖庫以二十人前驅，至中後所及山海關外诇敵，屢得邏卒，並獲其馬，又於前屯衛設伏敗敵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, Prince Rui Dorgon led an army against Ming and attacked Ningyuan; Xitu Ku with twenty men went ahead, scouted the enemy at Zhonghousuo and outside Shanhaiguan, repeatedly captured Ming deserters and seized their horses, and also set an ambush at Qiantunwei and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636), when Prince Rui Dorgon marched against the Ming and besieged Ningyuan, Xitu Ku rode ahead with twenty men, reconnoitered from Zhonghousuo to beyond Shanhaiguan, repeatedly picked off Ming scouts and their mounts, and laid an ambush at Qiantunwei that broke an enemy column.

sentences.zh: 喀木尼堪部葉類等盜科爾沁諸部馬叛走，錫圖庫率巴牙喇壯達八人詣寧古塔，與梅勒額真吳巴海督兵追之。

translations.literal: Yelei and others of the Kamnikhan tribe stole horses from the Khorchin tribes and fled in rebellion; Xitu Ku led eight bayara daitai to Ningguta and, with meiren ejen Ubai, directed troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelei of the Kamnikhan clan stole Khorchin horses and bolted, Xitu Ku took eight bayara lieutenants to Ningguta and, with meiren ejen Ubai, led the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 行數十日，及於溫鐸，招降不從，葉類潛遁，盡殲其黨九十四人，俘婦女八十餘，得馬五十六；

translations.literal: After marching several tens of days they reached Wende; when summons to surrender were refused, Yelei slipped away secretly, and they utterly destroyed his party of ninety-four men, captured more than eighty women, and obtained fifty-six horses;
translations.idiomatic: After weeks on the trail they caught up at Wende; Yelei refused parley and slipped away, but his band of ninety-four was wiped out, more than eighty women were taken, and fifty-six horses seized;

sentences.zh: 复逐捕葉類，入山，射之殪。

translations.literal: He again pursued and captured Yelei, entered the mountains, and shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: He then tracked Yelei into the hills and brought him down with an arrow.

sentences.zh: 師還，上遣大臣出迎五里，宴勞，進世職一等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor sent grand ministers to welcome them five li out, gave a feast to reward them, and advanced [Xitu Ku] to first-rank hereditary meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the emperor sent ministers five li out to receive them, feasted the column, and raised Xitu Ku to first-rank hereditary meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 五年，命偕巴牙喇纛章京濟什哈率師並徵蒙古敖漢、柰曼、烏喇特諸部兵伐索倫部，敗敵於甘河，擒部長博木博郭爾，籍千餘戶，得馬數百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered, together with bayara tuwakiyara janggin Jisika, to lead an army and jointly levy troops from the Mongol tribes of Aohan, Naiman, and Urad to campaign against the Solon; they defeated the enemy at Gan River, captured the chieftain Bombogor, registered more than a thousand households, and obtained several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1640) he and chief vanguard Jisika commanded a force that mustered Aohan, Naiman, and Urad auxiliaries against the Solon; at the Gan River they routed the foe, seized chieftain Bombogor, enrolled over a thousand households, and captured hundreds of horses.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜宴北驛館，進世職三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned, a feast was granted at the North Post Station, and he was advanced to third-rank hereditary angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they were feasted at the North Post Station and he was promoted to third-rank hereditary angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 旋授本旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed meiren ejen of his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named meiren ejen of his banner.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，自薊州越明都，下山東。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince Abatai in a campaign against Ming, passed from Jizhou across the Ming capital region, and descended into Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1642) he marched with Prince Abatai against the Ming, cutting south from Jizhou through the capital district into Shandong.

sentences.zh: 師還，以先出邊，部議當奪官，命寬之，白金百。

translations.literal: When the army returned, because he had left the border ahead of orders the board proposed stripping his office; the order was to pardon him, [with a fine of] one hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he was charged with crossing the border prematurely; although the board recommended dismissal, the throne pardoned him with a fine of one hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to bayara tuwakiyara janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1643) he was made chief bayara janggin.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從睿親王多爾袞伐明，敗李自成將唐通於一片石，遂入山海關，屢戰皆勝；

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Rui Dorgon in a campaign against Ming, defeated Li Zicheng's general Tang Tong at Yipianshi, then entered Shanhaiguan, and fought repeated battles, all victorious;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi (1644) he followed Prince Rui Dorgon south, routed Li Zicheng's general Tang Tong at Yipianshi, passed through Shanhaiguan, and won every engagement thereafter;

sentences.zh: 敗自成遊騎於三河，追擊至安肅。

translations.literal: He defeated Zicheng's roaming cavalry at Sanhe and pursued as far as Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Zicheng's scouting cavalry at Sanhe and chased the fugitives to Ansu.

sentences.zh: 旋從固山額真葉臣等取太原，戰於汾州、於絳州，屢破敵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed gushan ejen Yečen and others in taking Taiyuan, fought at Fenzhou and Jiangzhou, and repeatedly broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined banner commander Yečen in the capture of Taiyuan and repeatedly routed the enemy at Fenzhou and Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to second-rank jingqinihafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1645) he was raised to second-class jingqi nihafan.

sentences.zh: 時自成猶據陝西，師自潼關、綏德南北兩路入，錫圖庫率師與北路軍會，敗賊延安。

translations.literal: At that time Zicheng still held Shaanxi; the army entered by northern and southern routes through Tongguan and Suide; Xitu Ku led troops to join the northern-route army and defeated the bandits at Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: While Zicheng still held Shaanxi, imperial columns entered by the Tongguan and Suide corridors; Xitu Ku brought his detachment to the northern force and crushed the rebels at Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 自成走入湖廣，鍚圖庫移兵從之，自安陸至於荊門，屢擊敗自成兵。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled into Huguang; Xitu Ku shifted his army to follow him, and from Anlu to Jingmen repeatedly struck and defeated Zicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng fled into Huguang, Xitu Ku turned south in pursuit, harrying his columns from Anlu to Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 三年，復從肅親王豪格下四川，討張獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year he again followed Prince Su Hooge south into Sichuan to suppress Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1646) he marched under Prince Su Hooge into Sichuan against Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 五年，進世職一等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced one grade in hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1648) he gained a step in hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 復從鄭親王濟爾哈朗下湖南。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang south into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned in Hunan under Prince Zheng Jirhalang.

sentences.zh: 六年，師次長沙，錫圖庫從左翼巴牙喇纛章京努三率兵前驅，攻湘潭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the army halted at Changsha; Xitu Ku, following the left-wing bayara tuwakiyara janggin Nusan, led troops as vanguard and attacked Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1649), as the army paused at Changsha, he rode with left-wing chief vanguard Nusan ahead of the column to assault Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 努三軍北門，錫圖庫軍西門，遂克之。

translations.literal: Nusan's army at the north gate, Xitu Ku's army at the west gate — thus it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Nusan stormed the north gate while Xitu Ku struck the west, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 進徇永興，斬明將尹舉智、杜貞明等。

translations.literal: Advancing to sweep Yongxing, he beheaded the Ming generals Yin Juzhi, Du Zhenming, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Yongxing, he killed the Ming commanders Yin Juzhi and Du Zhenming, among others.

sentences.zh: 再進定寶慶，取全州，破明將焦璉。

translations.literal: Advancing further he secured Baoqing, took Quanzhou, and defeated the Ming general Jiao Lian.
translations.idiomatic: He next subdued Baoqing, seized Quanzhou, and broke the Ming general Jiao Lian.

sentences.zh: 又移兵克永安關，取道州。

translations.literal: He again shifted troops, captured Yong'anguan, and took Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting west he took Yong'an Pass and Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜白金三百。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted three hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he received a reward of three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 七年，睿親王多爾袞薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Rui Dorgon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1650) Prince Rui Dorgon died.

sentences.zh: 八年春，吳拜、羅什、博爾輝等訐英親王阿濟格將謀亂，鞫實，錫圖庫坐與謀，誅死，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, Wubai, Rosi, Bo Erhui, and others denounced Prince Ying Ajige for plotting rebellion; when the matter was examined and found true, Xitu Ku was convicted of complicity, executed, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year (1651) Wubai, Rosi, Bo Erhui, and others accused Prince Ying Ajige of plotting treason; Xitu Ku was found an accomplice, put to death, and his estate forfeited.

sentences.zh: =博爾輝=博爾輝，他塔喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Bo Erhui — Bo Erhui, of the Tatara clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Erhui, of the Tatara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初以巴牙喇壯達從征棟奎部，有俘馘。

translations.literal: At first, as a bayara daitai, he followed a campaign against the Dongkui tribe and took captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as bayara lieutenant in a campaign against the Dongkui and won captives and heads.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從太宗伐明，自龍井關入攻遵化。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed Taizong in a campaign against Ming, entered by Longjing Pass, and attacked Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancong (1629) he joined Hong Taiji's Ming expedition, entered through Longjing Pass, and assaulted Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 明總兵趙率教自山海關赴援，與戰，博爾輝斬其副將，明兵驚潰。

translations.literal: Ming regional commander Zhao Shuaijiao came from Shanhaiguan to relieve the city; in battle Bo Erhui beheaded his deputy commander, and the Ming army fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming commander Zhao Shuaijiao marched from Shanhaiguan to relieve the city, Bo Erhui slew his deputy and sent the Ming force fleeing in disorder.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢巴牙喇甲喇章京，兼戶部參政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to bayara jalan janggin and concurrently served as a councillor of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1631) he was made bayara jalan janggin and also sat on the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 復從伐明，與明兵遇寧遠，擊殺前隊七人。

translations.literal: He again followed a campaign against Ming; encountering Ming troops at Ningyuan, he struck and killed seven of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On another Ming campaign he met enemy troops at Ningyuan and killed seven in the forward line.

sentences.zh: 八年，復從伐明，攻大同，明兵三千自龍門迎戰，博爾輝與噶布什賢章京錫特庫、牛錄額真星訥等奮擊破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again followed a campaign against Ming and attacked Datong; three thousand Ming troops came from Longmen to offer battle; Bo Erhui, with Gabsihiyan janggin Sitku and niru commander Singne and others, fought fiercely and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1634), during the assault on Datong, he and Gabsihiyan commander Sitku and niru captain Singne shattered three thousand Ming troops advancing from Longmen.

sentences.zh: 九年，命偕承政馬福塔齎敕諭朝鮮國王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered, together with cheng'e Mafuta, to carry an imperial edict and instruct the King of Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1635) he was sent with cheng'e Mafuta to deliver an edict to the Korean king.

sentences.zh: 師出邊招察哈爾部眾，自歸化經明邊東還，博爾輝殿。

translations.literal: When the army went out to the border to summon the Chahar tribes' people, returning east along the Ming border from Guihua, Bo Erhui formed the rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: On a border mission to summon Chahar clans, he commanded the rearguard on the return march east from Guihua along the Ming frontier.

sentences.zh: 明兵二百三十追擊我師，博爾輝以二十人擊卻之，斬十人，俘一人，得馬三。

translations.literal: Two hundred thirty Ming troops pursued and attacked our army; Bo Erhui with twenty men drove them back, beheaded ten, captured one, and obtained three horses.
translations.idiomatic: When 230 Ming soldiers pursued the column, Bo Erhui turned with twenty men, killed ten, took one prisoner, and seized three horses.

sentences.zh: 明兵從我師，有垂為所獲者，博爾輝救之得脫。

translations.literal: Ming troops followed our army; some were on the verge of being captured; Bo Erhui rescued them and they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As Ming skirmishers pressed the rearguard he rescued men about to be taken and brought them off safely.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，敘功，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when merits were reckoned, he was granted a hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636) his service was rewarded with a hereditary niru janggin rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，裁參政，專任巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the third year the concurrent councillor post was abolished, and he served solely as bayara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1638) he left the revenue board to serve full time as bayara jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，兼任刑部理事官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was concurrently appointed an executive official of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi (1644) he also held an executive post on the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 從入關，擊李自成，敘功，進世職二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Following the entry through the passes, he struck Li Zicheng; when merits were reckoned, he was advanced to second-rank hereditary jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the passes he fought Li Zicheng and was raised to second-rank hereditary jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 旋署巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he acted as bayara tuwakiyara janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting chief bayara janggin.

sentences.zh: 從順承郡王勒克德渾下湖廣，師至武昌。

translations.literal: Following Prince Shuncheng Lekdehun south into Huguang, the army reached Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Huguang with Prince Shuncheng Lekdehun and the army halted at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時自成將馬進忠、王進才既降复叛，據岳州，​​令博爾輝率師討之，次臨湘，擊敗其兵。

translations.literal: At that time Zicheng's generals Ma Jinzhong and Wang Jincai, having surrendered and again rebelled, held Yuezhou; [the court] ordered Bo Erhui to lead troops to suppress them; halting at Linxiang, he struck and defeated their army.
translations.idiomatic: When the former rebel generals Ma Jinzhong and Wang Jincai, who had submitted and rebelled again, held Yuezhou, Bo Erhui was sent against them and routed their force at Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 進攻岳州，進忠、進才走長沙，逐擊敗之，其將黑運昌以舟師降。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yuezhou, Jinzhong and Jincai fled to Changsha; he pursued, struck, and defeated them; their general Hei Yunchang surrendered with his fleet.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Yuezhou; when Jinzhong and Jincai fled to Changsha he hunted them down, and their admiral Hei Yunchang surrendered his river flotilla.

sentences.zh: 師還，優賚。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was generously rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 五年，真除巴牙喇纛章京，列議政大臣，進世職二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was permanently appointed bayara tuwakiyara janggin, listed among the deliberative grand ministers, and advanced to second-rank hereditary ashanihafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1648) he was confirmed chief bayara janggin, given a seat among the regency council, and promoted to second-class ashanihafan.

sentences.zh: 睿親王攝政，諸王多與忤。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui served as regent, many princes were at odds with him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Rui's regency many princes fell out with him.

sentences.zh: 鄭親王濟爾哈朗降郡王，旋复爵。

translations.literal: Prince Zheng Jirhalang was reduced to the rank of commandery prince, then quickly had his peerage restored.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zheng Jirhalang was demoted to commandery prince, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 初以端重親王博洛、敬謹親王尼堪佐理事，亦以專擅降爵。

translations.literal: At first Prince Duoduo Boluo and Prince Jing Niken assisted in governing affairs, but they too were reduced in rank for arrogating authority.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Boluo and Niken, who had initially helped govern, were likewise demoted for acting on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 博爾輝及諸大臣羅什、額克親、吳拜、蘇拜皆謹事睿親王，從王獵喀喇城。

translations.literal: Bo Erhui and the grand ministers Rosi, Ekqin, Wubai, and Subai all dutifully served Prince Rui and followed the Prince hunting at Kala Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Erhui, Rosi, Ekqin, Wubai, and Subai all curried favor with the regent and joined his hunt at Kala Castle.

sentences.zh: 王薨，喪還。

translations.literal: The Prince died; the mourning party returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince died the funeral cortège returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 英親王阿濟格為睿親王同母兄，欲繼王柄政，博爾輝等與阿爾津共發其罪，英親王奪爵幽禁，賞諸告者，博爾輝進世職二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Ajige, Prince Rui's elder brother by the same mother, wished to succeed the Prince in holding power; Bo Erhui and others together with A'erjin exposed his crimes; Prince Ying was stripped of his peerage and imprisoned; the accusers were rewarded, and Bo Erhui was advanced to second-rank hereditary jingqinihafan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Ajige—Dorgon's elder brother—sought to seize the regency; Bo Erhui and A'erjin denounced him; Ajige was disgraced and imprisoned, the accusers were rewarded, and Bo Erhui rose to second-class jingqi nihafan.

sentences.zh: 博爾輝等傳睿親王遺言，复理事二王親王爵，以告兩黃旗大臣。

translations.literal: Bo Erhui and others transmitted Prince Rui's deathbed words, restoring Boluo and Niken to prince rank in governing affairs, and reported this to the grand ministers of the two Yellow Banners.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Erhui and his allies claimed Dorgon's dying wish to restore Boluo and Niken as princes and told the Yellow Banner ministers.

sentences.zh: 居月餘，命未下，博爾輝有疾，穆爾泰往視之，博爾輝以為言。

translations.literal: After more than a month the order had not come down; Bo Erhui was ill; Mu'ertai went to visit him, and Bo Erhui spoke of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed without an edict; when Bo Erhui fell ill and Mu'ertai called on him, he confided his grievance.

sentences.zh: 穆爾泰告額爾德赫，額爾德赫告敬謹郡王尼堪，遂與端重郡王博洛訴於鄭親王。

translations.literal: Mu'ertai told E'erdehe; E'erdehe told Prince Jing Niken; thus together with Prince Duoduo Boluo they appealed to Prince Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mu'ertai told E'erdehe, who told Prince Niken; Niken and Prince Boluo then brought the complaint to Prince Zheng.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，复二王爵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the two princes' peerages were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year (1651) Boluo and Niken were restored to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 越八日，執博爾輝等下獄，坐博爾輝、羅什動搖國事，蠱惑人心，論死，籍其家。

translations.literal: Eight days later Bo Erhui and others were seized and imprisoned; Bo Erhui and Rosi were convicted of shaking state affairs and bewitching people's hearts, sentenced to death, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later Bo Erhui and his circle were arrested; Bo Erhui and Rosi were condemned for subverting the state and poisoning public opinion, sentenced to death, and their estates seized.

sentences.zh: 額克親削宗室籍，及吳拜、蘇拜皆奪官為民。

translations.literal: Ekqin was struck from the imperial clan register; Wubai and Subai were all stripped of office and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Ekqin was expunged from the Aisin Gioro rolls; Wubai and Subai were cashiered to common status.

sentences.zh: 議上，得旨：「朕每聞刑人，殊不忍。

translations.literal: When the deliberations were submitted, an edict came: "Whenever I hear of punishing men, I feel deeply reluctant.
translations.idiomatic: When the sentence went up for review, the emperor replied: "I am always loath to hear of executions.

sentences.zh: 二人罪當誅，姑宥死何如？

translations.literal: These two men's crimes merit death — how about pardoning them from death for the time being?
translations.idiomatic: These two deserve death—might we spare them for now?

sentences.zh: 」王大臣復以初議上，乃誅死。

translations.literal: " The princes and grand ministers resubmitted the original recommendation, and [the two] were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The princes and ministers resubmitted the original verdict, and the two were put to death.

sentences.zh: =冷僧機=冷僧機，納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人，葉赫部長金台石之族也。

translations.literal: Leng Sengji — Leng Sengji, of the Nara clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, of the lineage of Gintaisi, chieftain of the Yehe tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Sengji, of the Nara clan, was a Plain Yellow Banner Manchu and a kinsman of Yehe chieftain Gintaisi.

sentences.zh: 葉赫亡，來歸，隸正藍旗，屬貝勒莽古爾泰。

translations.literal: When Yehe perished he came to submit, was assigned to the Plain Blue Banner, and belonged to Prince Mang'ertai.
translations.idiomatic: After Yehe fell he submitted, entered the Plain Blue Banner, and served under Prince Mang'ertai.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，敖漢部長索諾木來歸，尚公主為額駙，以冷僧機隸焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong the Aohan chieftain Sonom came to submit, married a princess as efu (imperial son-in-law), and Leng Sengji was assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancong (1627) Aohan chief Sonom submitted, married an imperial princess, and Leng Sengji was transferred to his household.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰既卒，九年，冷僧機詣法司言莽古爾泰及貝勒德格類與公主及索諾木結黨，設誓謀不軌。

translations.literal: After Mang'ertai had died, in the ninth year Leng Sengji went to the legal bureau and reported that Mang'ertai and Prince Degesi, together with the princess and Sonom, formed a faction, swore oaths, and plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: After Mang'ertai's death, in the ninth year (1635) Leng Sengji went to the judicial authorities and accused Mang'ertai and Prince Degesi of forming a clique with the princess and Sonom and swearing treasonous oaths.

sentences.zh: 冷僧機與甲喇額真屯布祿、巴克什愛巴禮並下法司，鞫實，冷僧機以自首免罪，屯布祿、​​愛巴禮皆坐誅，籍其家以★K2冷僧機，改隸正黃旗，授世職三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Leng Sengji with jalan commander Tunbulu and baksi Aibali were all sent down to the legal bureau; when examined and found true, Leng Sengji was exempted from punishment for self-reporting; Tunbulu and Aibali were both executed, their households were confiscated and given to Leng Sengji; he was reassigned to the Plain Yellow Banner and granted a third-rank hereditary meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Sengji, jalan commander Tunbulu, and secretary Aibali were all examined; Leng Sengji was spared for confessing first, while Tunbulu and Aibali were executed and their households confiscated and given to Leng Sengji; he was transferred to the Plain Yellow Banner as third-rank hereditary meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，固山額真都類坐事下兵部待鞫，兵部參政穆爾泰令諸在系者避都類。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde, gushan ejen Dulei, convicted of an offense, was sent down to the Board of War to await examination; Board councillor Mu'ertai ordered all those in custody to avoid Dulei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongde (1637), when banner commander Dulei was detained at the War Board pending trial, board councillor Mu'ertai ordered other prisoners to keep away from him.

sentences.zh: 或以告冷僧機，聞於上，穆爾泰及同官皆坐降罰，授冷僧機一等侍衛。

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Leng Sengji; it reached the emperor; Mu'ertai and his colleagues were all punished with demotion; Leng Sengji was appointed a first-class guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Leng Sengji reported the favoritism, Mu'ertai and his colleagues were demoted and Leng Sengji was made a first-class guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，祖大壽來歸，上幸牧馬所，命內大臣侍衛與大壽等校射，中的者有所賜，冷僧機得駝一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Zu Dashou came to submit; the emperor visited the horse pastures, ordered inner grand ministers and guards to compete in archery with Dashou and others; those who hit the mark received rewards, and Leng Sengji obtained one camel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1642), when Zu Dashou surrendered, the emperor held an archery contest at the horse farm; Leng Sengji hit the mark and won a camel.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，授內大臣。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was appointed inner grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shunzhi emperor's accession he became an inner grand minister.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，進二等阿思哈尼哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was advanced to second-rank ashanihafan, concurrently holding tuwalarahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi (1645) he rose to second-class ashanihafan with tuwalarahafan.

sentences.zh: 譚泰訐索尼，引冷僧機為證，謝未聞，坐徇庇，當削世職籍沒，上貰之。

translations.literal: Tan Tai denounced Sony, citing Leng Sengji as witness; [Leng Sengji] pleaded he had not heard; convicted of shielding [Tan Tai], he ought to have been stripped of hereditary office and his property confiscated; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Tai accused Sony and Leng Sengji was called as witness, Leng Sengji claimed ignorance; though shielding Tan Tai should have cost him his rank and property, the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 旋進世職三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was advanced to third-rank hereditary jingqinihafan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to third-class jingqi nihafan.

sentences.zh: 七年，睿親王有疾，怨上未臨視，冷僧機及貝子錫翰等奏請上臨視，睿親王坐以擅請降世職，恩詔復故，進一等伯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Rui was ill and resented that the emperor had not come to visit; Leng Sengji and Beile Xihan and others memorialized asking the emperor to pay a visit; in the affair of unauthorized petition Leng Sengji was convicted and reduced in hereditary rank; by an amnesty edict his rank was restored and he was advanced to first-rank bo (marquis).
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1650), when the ailing Prince Rui resented the emperor's failure to visit, Leng Sengji and Beile Xihan petitioned for an imperial visit; Leng Sengji was demoted for the improper petition, but an amnesty restored his rank and raised him to first-class marquis.

sentences.zh: 睿親王薨，以豫親王多鐸子多爾博為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui died, Dorgon's son Dorbo of Prince Yu was made his heir and inherited the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Rui's death Dorbo, son of Prince Yu Dodo, was adopted as his heir and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 冷僧機言於上曰：「昔太宗登遐，兩黃旗大臣誓立肅親王。

translations.literal: Leng Sengji said to the emperor: "Formerly, when Taizong passed away, the grand ministers of the two Yellow Banners swore to enthrone Prince Su.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Sengji told the emperor: "When Hong Taiji died the Yellow Banner ministers swore to raise Prince Su Hooge.

sentences.zh: 睿親王定策奉上紹統，多爾博宜特見優遇。

translations.literal: Prince Rui settled the plan and presented Your Majesty to inherit the succession; Dorbo ought especially to receive favored treatment."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui chose you for the throne; Dorbo deserves special favor."

sentences.zh: 」又舉侍衛羅什，羅什上為冷僧機乞恩。

translations.literal: He also recommended the guard Rosi; Rosi memorialized the throne asking grace for Leng Sengji.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended guard Rosi, who petitioned the throne on Leng Sengji's behalf.

sentences.zh: 八年，鄭親王濟爾哈朗等劾羅什蠱惑諸王，坐誅，辭連冷僧機。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Prince Zheng Jirhalang and others impeached Rosi for bewitching the princes; he was convicted and executed; his testimony implicated Leng Sengji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1651) Prince Zheng Jirhalang charged Rosi with swaying the princes; Rosi was executed, implicating Leng Sengji.

sentences.zh: 上因命諸大臣詰誓立肅親王事，冷僧機窮，諸大臣兼發阿諛睿親王諸罪，論斬籍沒，命寬之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore ordered the grand ministers to interrogate [Leng Sengji] on the matter of swearing to enthrone Prince Su; Leng Sengji was cornered; the grand ministers also exposed his crimes of flattery toward Prince Rui; he was sentenced to execution and confiscation of property; the order was to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ministers interrogate him about the oath to enthrone Prince Su; cornered, he faced further charges of fawning on Prince Rui; though condemned to death with forfeiture, the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 九年，追論冷僧機與貝子鞏阿岱、錫翰，內大臣西訥布庫等迎合睿親王，亂國政，下王大臣鞫實，與鞏阿岱、錫翰、西訥布庫等並誅，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Leng Sengji was again tried together with Beile Gong'adai, Xihan, inner grand minister Xinabuku, and others for currying favor with Prince Rui and disordering state affairs; sent down to the princes and grand ministers for examination and found true; together with Gong'adai, Xihan, Xinabuku, and others he was executed, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1652) he was tried again with Beile Gong'adai, Xihan, and inner minister Xinabuku for colluding with Prince Rui to corrupt government; all were executed and their estates seized.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：定金聲桓、王得仁之亂，譚泰專將，何洛會為之佐。

translations.literal: [Discussion] The Discussion says: In settling the rebellion of Jin Shenghuan and Wang Deren, Tan Tai was sole commander and Heluohui served as his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: In quelling Jin Shenghuan and Wang Deren's revolt, Tan Tai commanded alone with Heluohui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 錫圖庫、博爾輝亦久從征戰有勞。

translations.literal: Xitu Ku and Bo Erhui also for long followed campaigns and warfare with labor and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xitu Ku and Bo Erhui had likewise served long in the field with distinction.

sentences.zh: 睿親王既薨，諸阿附者乃互相傾，何洛會之獄，譚泰證之；

translations.literal: After Prince Rui had died, those who had attached themselves to him then turned against one another; in Heluohui's case, Tan Tai testified against him;
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Rui's death his former clients turned on one another: Tan Tai testified in Heluohui's trial;

sentences.zh: 錫圖庫之誅，博爾輝等發之：轉相排軋，同就誅夷。

translations.literal: Xitu Ku's execution was initiated by Bo Erhui and others: turning to mutual persecution, they alike met execution and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: and Bo Erhui's faction denounced Xitu Ku—each faction informing on the other until all were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 若冷僧機者，專事告訐，其及也亦宜矣。

translations.literal: As for one like Leng Sengji, who devoted himself to denunciation, that he too met ruin was also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Sengji, who lived by accusation, richly deserved the same fate.
